A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LRAM study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering, including identical retained plot images.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E report original multi-domain evaluations, fine-tuning, Dark-Room in-context learning, inference measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds controlled ablations, action-smoothness measurements, and per-task results in Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same recurrent backbones, action-free state/RTG/reward sequences, shared discretized action head, cross-entropy objective, and recurrent inference procedure. Token-removal and block-composition alternatives are introduced as ablation conditions, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six-domain mixture of 432 training tasks, 37 held-out tasks, and Dark-Room 10 × 10 with 80 training and 20 held-out goals. The added studies reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding backbone comparisons retain DT, Mamba, xLSTM [1:0], and xLSTM [7:1]; fine-tuning still compares pretrained and randomly initialized xLSTMs. New behavior-cloning comparisons use the same backbones. Additional block ratios are internal ablations, while newly cited decision-model papers are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds full-mixture action/context sweeps, controlled removal of RTG or RTG plus reward tokens, and block-ratio and placement sweeps. These substantially expand experimental configurations while retaining the original main training and evaluation protocol. The ratio study has inconsistent size reporting: 16M in Appendix E.3 versus 206M in Figure 29's caption.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's Meta-World action-history, dropout, and layer-count ablations, v2 tests action history across all 432 tasks, adds xLSTM context-length sweeps and adjacent-action MSE analysis, and investigates return conditioning and block composition/placement on the task mixture and Dark-Room (Appendix E, Figures 23–30).

E5.justification: The existing three-seed means and 95% confidence intervals, and single-run 408M qualification, are retained. V2 specifies single-seed exceptions for new full-task DT context and block-ratio sweeps and reports standard deviations for adjacent-action MSE in Table 7. This does not establish changed run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained plots are unchanged, but Figures 23–30 and Tables 7–16 add substantial results. New action-free context sweeps report normalized scores rising approximately from 0.3 to 0.7 for DT and 0.4 to 0.8 for xLSTM as context increases from 1 to 50. Appendix G adds per-task scores at the 206M scale.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, trajectory definitions, and conditioning equations (1)–(2) remain unchanged. V2 adds empirical and conceptual discussion without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: xLSTM-based LRAM, favorable performance and inference efficiency, evaluation of fine-tuning and in-context learning, and dataset/pipeline release. The new controls support these existing headline claims.

C2.justification: V2 develops a domain-specific copycat explanation tied to action smoothness and explains when sLSTM state tracking and layer placement help. Section 5 adds Transformer exact-recall advantages and task-dependent backbone selection, including the relevance of less powerful edge hardware. Existing real-robot, offline-fine-tuning, and grid-world limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly explains extracting environment-specific action dimensions from joint predictions, and Appendix A states that source code accompanies the submission. V1's explicit full-fine-tuning disclosure is omitted. Most implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and the repository location are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ota and Dai et al. on Mamba-based decision models, Wen et al. on copycat behavior, and Ni et al. on memory/recall. It removes Di Palo et al. and selected fine-tuning and ICL references. These are targeted contextual updates rather than a wholesale repositioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable. V2 makes local rewrites, expands the ablation subsection hierarchy, renames the ethics statement, moves reproducibility from Section 7 to Appendix A, removes the appendix contents list, and updates affiliation text.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure resizing and relocation. V1's separate memory plot becomes Figure 6c in v2. Eight new ablation figures, the action-MSE table, and nine raw-score tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for important design choices. V1's action-history justification relied mainly on a Meta-World ablation; v2 tests the full task mixture, measures action smoothness, and checks return-conditioning and block-composition alternatives. Per-task scores and task-dependent qualifications make the retained claims easier to scrutinize. Single-seed sweeps and the Figure 29 model-size inconsistency limit parts of the added evidence but do not outweigh these gains.
